audit.report: Card settlement blocked checkout because pid 112734 held a lock while idle in transaction for 4 seconds. The Database Guardian proposed waiting instead of terminating the protected, non-replayable card_settlement job, which carries $12,500 in flight and risks double charges or lost settlements if interrupted. The Continuity Guardian accepted because waiting cost about $2,561 and fit within the business-tolerated 60-second degradation window. The blocker finished on its own after 23 seconds, and verification confirmed recovery: 36/36 checkouts succeeded over 10 seconds (100% vs 95% SLO), no lock waits remain, and protected settlements are intact. The business is back.
audit.root_cause: The card_settlement protected settlement job (pid 112734) was idle in transaction and blocked checkout sessions, degrading success from 92% to 80% before the wait resolved.
lessons: For card_settlement, check the workload registry for replayable=False and policy never_interrupt before proposing any kill; terminating it risks double charges or lost settlements on in-flight amounts.
audit.negotiation_critique: Neither guardian wasted a round; the Database Guardian gathered registry, calendar, and impact evidence before confirming wait, and the Continuity Guardian accepted with no objection. No invariant overrode the negotiation.
follow_ups: Investigate why settlement_worker pid 112734 went idle in transaction while holding locks and add monitoring to alert when a protected transaction exceeds a safe threshold.
Confirm with Payments whether card_settlement should have a defined interrupt or retry policy so future blockages can be resolved faster without risking the $12,500 in flight.
